newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Caltex Philippines extends turnaround, ups imports.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Philippines extends turnaround, ups imports.

text.p: Caltex (Phils) Inc, a unit of the joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, has extended the maintenance of its 35,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) by two days, a company source said.
The unit was due to restart on Tuesday. The source did not give any reason for the delay.
The CDU's scheduled turnaround began January 20, along with three secondary refining units.
He said the maintenance for a 9,000-bpd platformer due only to return at the end of the month, has been shortened and was currently being restarted, together with a 16,000-bpd naphtha treater.
A 14,000-bpd diesel desulphuriser, which users the hydrogen produced from the platformer, would start in three to four days time.
The source said the two-day extension of CDU shutdown would not prompt additional product demand, as Caltex has already stepped up its its gasoline and gas oil imports for January and February.
Caltex normally imports around 100,000 barrels per month of 95-octane unleaded gasoline, but for Janaury it imported 100,000 barrels of reformate and 83,000 barrels of gasoline, the source said.
"Although we regularly import reformate or finished gasoline, February imports will be slightly higher because of the shutdown," said the source.

In February, it has bought two cargoes totalling 150,000 barrels at $2.75 to $3.16 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Batangas where Caltex runs its 70,000-bpd refinery.
Similarly, Caltex has increased its usual monthly gas oil purchases of around 250,000 barrels.
In January, it imported 230,000 barrels of gas oil but bought 60,000 barrels domestically from fellow refiner Shell.
For February, it has bought around 380,000 barrels from Singapore and South Korea at a premium of $1.05 per barrel over Singapore spot gas oil quotes, c-and-f Batangas.
Caltex usually buys its requirements from its Singapore affiliate in Singapore who sources the cargoes from its refineries in Singapore, Thailand and South Korea.
